entries.title: 을사보호조약의 효력을 둘러싼 논쟁: 주한 러시아 총영사의 인가장 문제에서 나타난 러일 외교 갈등 [The Contested Validity of the Eulsa Protectorate Treaty: Diplomatic Tensions over the Exequatur for the Russian Consul-General in Korea]
entries.venue: 인문논총 [Journal of Humanities, Institute of Humanities, Seoul National University]
entries.summary: Argues that the international acceptance of Korea's protectorate status after 1905 was never legally self-evident but had to be politically manufactured, and reconstructs that process through the Russo-Japanese quarrel over who could issue the exequatur for Russia's Consul-General to Korea, G. A. Planson. Song contends that trying to prove the treaty's illegality by the standards of an imperialist-era international law paradoxically risks legitimating Japan's conduct; the more revealing evidence is Japan's own anxiety that the treaty might fail to win third-party recognition, and the fact that both Tokyo and St Petersburg mobilized diplomatic networks to sound out the great powers. Validity, she concludes, was decided at the boundary between international law and great-power politics rather than by legal form alone.

entries.title: Global Human Rights Institutions
entries.venue: The Sage Handbook of Peace and Conflict Studies, eds. Maia Carter Hallward, Ji Eun Kim, Cecile Mouly, Timothy Seidel and Zubairu Wai (Sage, June 2025), Part 4: Global Issues, Institutions, and Change
entries.summary: A peer-reviewed handbook chapter surveying the global architecture of human rights institutions within the handbook's explicitly de-Westernizing agenda, which sets out to correct the field's Euro-American centre of gravity by foregrounding Global South perspectives on violence, conflict, and peace. NOTE: the chapter's specific argument could not be read -- Sage Knowledge is behind a login -- so this describes the chapter's placement and remit rather than its thesis; chapter number 39 and co-authorship with Chaeyoung Yong are confirmed, authorship is alphabetical.

entries.title: Treaty-Making and Colonization in East Asia: Vietnam and Korea in the 19th Century
entries.venue: Ph.D. dissertation, Department of Political Science, University of Florida
entries.summary: Argues that the nineteenth-century treaties Vietnam and Korea concluded with Western powers did not simply admit two Asian polities into international society but supplied the legal instrument through which the pre-existing East Asian regional order was dismantled and colonization was authorized. By comparing the two cases, the project treats the European treaty system as a mechanism of legal imperialism rather than a neutral form of recognition, and traces how sovereignty was redefined for polities entering it from within the 'Chinese world order'. Research rests on archival work at the New York Public Library, the National Archives (London) and the National Institute of Korean History.

entries.title: 인도태평양 시대 유엔과 동북아시아의 정당성 경쟁 [The United Nations in the Indo-Pacific Era and Competition for Legitimacy in East Asia]
entries.venue: 통일과 평화 [Journal of Peace and Unification Studies], Institute for Peace and Unification Studies, Seoul National University
entries.summary: Argues from a social-constructivist standpoint that Northeast Asian states are all 'incomplete' sovereigns by the modern Western measure -- internally rival states (China/Taiwan, South/North Korea) and an 'abnormal state' (Japan) -- and that they have therefore waged a sustained competition for legitimacy inside the UN to win international recognition. Analyzing Security Council records, UN General Assembly keynote addresses, and official statements by permanent representatives and foreign ministers, Kwon shows that all five parties strategically deploy the UN Charter as the organization's core symbolic resource to legitimize themselves and delegitimize rivals over membership and permanent Security Council seats, with China in particular fusing Charter-based non-interference with an insistence on 'Chinese-style' solutions.

entries.title: Blacklisted Rebels: Commitment to Child Rights in Armed Conflict
entries.venue: Ph.D. dissertation, Department of Political Science, University of Notre Dame (committee: Gary Goertz, Tanisha M. Fazal, Emilia Justyna Powell)
entries.summary: Argues against the field's working assumption that a rebel group's non-use of child soldiers signals genuine commitment to international humanitarian law -- some groups simply never had the incentive or lacked alternatives. Studying all groups blacklisted by the UN for child rights violations between 2002 and 2018 across four sequential phases (violating, listing, signing UN action plans, complying), and combining large-N statistics, QCA on medium-N cases, and congruence tests on small-N cases, Kwon argues first that rebels weigh their legitimacy before domestic and international audiences at every phase, and second that a host state's own motive to blacklist its rebels is the key factor driving whether the UN lists a given group. The dissertation bridges the international-institutions and political-violence literatures and carries policy implications for protecting children in armed conflict.

entries.title: '민족자결'의 수용과 2·8 독립운동 [Translation of 'Self-determination' and the Feb. 8th Independence Movement]
entries.venue: 한국동양정치사상사연구 [The Review of Korean and Asian Political Thoughts]
entries.summary: Argues that the February 8th (1919) movement by Korean students in Tokyo was not naive Wilsonianism but a calculated legal-political manoeuvre. Song points to two anomalies — the petition went to the Japanese government and Diet rather than to Washington, London or Paris, and it demanded a 'National Convention' (民族大會) rather than independence outright — and shows both follow the procedure laid down in Point 5 of the Fourteen Points, whose test of 'the interests of the populations concerned' the petition met by documenting Korean loss under Japanese rule. Since the students' own speeches and their journal Hakjigwang show they already knew self-determination would not be extended to Korea, she reads the movement as a deliberate attempt to stretch the scope of the Fourteen Points: what Western IR historiography files under idealism was, in colonial Korea, the most realistic option available.

entries.title: 근대 한국의 민족자결 '수용'과 2.8 독립운동 [Translation of 'Self-determination' by Modern Korea and the Feb. 8th Independence Movement]
entries.venue: M.A. thesis, Department of Diplomacy (외교학과), Graduate School, Seoul National University (74 pp.)
entries.summary: The master's thesis from which her 2012 article derives: it reconstructs how Korean students in Tokyo received and repurposed the Wilsonian language of self-determination, arguing that their petition strategy in the February 8th movement was shaped by a working reading of the Fourteen Points rather than by an uncritical faith in Wilson.

themes.title: Emotion, Trauma, and Memory
themes.blurb: Treats affect as a political practice with a history of its own — anger organized in the streets of 1960 Tokyo, deference performed across a negotiating table, the time structure of traumatic memory in testimony about wartime sexual violence — and asks what emotion studies becomes once non-Western voices are inside it rather than cited by it.

entries.title: Emotional practices of anger: the case of the anti-Japan-US security treaty (Anpo) protests (1959-60)
entries.venue: Cambridge Review of International Affairs
entries.summary: Argues that anger in the 1959-60 Anpo protests should be read not as an irrational outburst but as an emotional practice: protesters performed anger to signal how serious the treaty issue was to them, to name specific injustices, and to demand action. Combining practice theory with frame analysis, it shows that injustice frames drawn from war memory and from democratic procedure supplied the rationale that made anger politically legible, and that these angry practices reshaped the terms of Japan's foreign and security policy debate.

entries.title: Trauma Time and Memory in Understanding Gender-Based Violence
entries.venue: Millennium: Journal of International Studies (special issue 'Traversing Memories in Global Politics')
entries.summary: Takes Jenny Edkins' concept of 'trauma time' out of its usual state-violence setting and argues that it illuminates gender-based violence by exposing trauma as socio-political rather than merely individual, and by disrupting the linear narrative of healing and restored social order. Through the UK's Gender Recognition Reform Bill debates it shows that gender-critical feminists and trans rights activists both invoke trauma time, but that only the latter's enactment troubles the linear temporality that conceals multiple, overlapping sites of violence.

entries.title: The dynamics of anger in protests and security debates in Japan (1948-1960)
entries.venue: PhD thesis, School of International Relations, University of St Andrews (supervisors K. M. Fierke and Chris Ogden)
entries.summary: Asks how and why protesters in post-war Japan expressed anger over foreign and security policy, across three episodes: opposition to rearmament during the Korean War, resistance to the San Francisco Peace Treaty and the Japan-US Security Treaty in 1952, and the 1959-60 anti-treaty demonstrations. Using emotion discourse analysis, it argues that anger was deployed to mark the seriousness of the issue, to name injustices, and to contest the dominant national security narrative, and that in doing so it shaped the foreign policymaking debate itself.

entries.title: Global emotion studies in IR: embracing non-Western voices
entries.venue: Going beyond Parochialism and Fragmentation in the Study of International Relations, ed. Yong-Soo Eun (Routledge, IR Theory and Practice in Asia series)
entries.summary: Argues that the emotions turn in IR has reproduced the very parochialism it claims to escape, because its conceptual vocabulary of emotion is drawn almost entirely from Western philosophical and psychological traditions. Contends that a genuinely global study of emotion requires actively incorporating non-Western understandings of feeling, and sets out what such incorporation would change - both what Western-centric approaches have neglected and what pluralising the ontology of emotion would yield for IR theory.

entries.authors: 은용수, 용채영 [Yong-Soo Eun and Chaeyoung Yong]
entries.title: 국제정치학 감정연구의 쟁점, 함의, 그리고 향배 [Taking Stock of Emotion Studies in IR: Where Do We Stand and Where Are We Heading?]
entries.venue: 『세계정치』 제29호: 감정의 세계, 정치 [World Politics 29: The World of Emotions, Politics], ed. 은용수 (서울대학교 국제문제연구소 / 사회평론아카데미)
entries.summary: Reviews the emotions literature in IR theoretically and methodologically and argues that emotion possesses both individual and collective (micro and macro) ontological dimensions, neither of which should be given analytic priority. Identifies the central unresolved task as explaining how individual feeling becomes collectivised and politicised, proposes concepts for linking emotion to power politics, and claims that emotion research has practical value in generating the empathy required for reconciliation and peacebuilding between states and ethnic groups.

entries.authors: 용채영, 은용수 [Chaeyoung Yong and Yong-Soo Eun]
entries.title: 국제정치학(IR)의 감정연구: 비판적 검토와 이론적 제언 [Emotion Studies in IR: Critical Review and Theoretical Suggestion]
entries.venue: 국제정치논총 [The Korean Journal of International Relations]
entries.summary: Attacks the emotion-versus-reason binary inherited from Western thought and argues that emotion is simultaneously a universal human capacity and a socio-culturally particular one, so that it cannot be located at either the individual or the collective level alone. Identifies 'affective politics' - how emotions are triggered in political settings and mobilised by elites - as the field's main blind spot, and proposes a reflectivist research agenda in which emotion research strengthens IR theory and supports empathy-based reconciliation and peacebuilding.

themes.title: Ways of Knowing: How IR Knowledge Is Made and Moves
themes.blurb: The collective's reflexive core: what counts as knowledge of the international, who assembles it, and how it travels. It runs from relational philosophy of social science (knowing-from-within, relationalism as labour against the grain of scholarly writing) to the archival history of Korean IR's own founding — Lee Yong-hee as bricoleur, Cho Hyowon's rival Cold War realism, the Koreanization worked through the early KAIS conferences — and on to the institutions, translations and networks through which imported concepts were localized.

entries.authors: Patrick Thaddeus Jackson and Sujin Heo
entries.title: Ways of Knowing
entries.venue: Berit Bliesemann de Guevara, Katarzyna Kaczmarska, Xymena Kurowska, Birgit Poopuu and Andrea Warnecke (eds.), Knowledge and Expertise in International Politics: A Handbook (Oxford University Press)
entries.summary: Argues that the question of epistemic authority in world politics cannot be settled without first drawing careful conceptual distinctions among kinds of knowledge. The chapter separates knowing-that (facts) from know-how (skills), then subjects that typology to a relational critique and introduces a third kind — 'knowing-from-within,' the relational capacity to go on appropriately inside a context that brings the judgements of others to bear through a community of practice. It contends that scholarly, expert, and practitioner knowledges alike are generated through this relational knowing-from-within rather than through detached representation of an external world.

entries.title: 강만길 지정학의 지정학 [Searching for a Geopolitical Equilibrium between Land Power and Sea Power in East Asia: Focusing on Kang Man-Gil's Geopolitical Ideas]
entries.venue: 한국사학보 (The Journal for the Studies of Korean History)
entries.summary: Argues that the historian Kang Man-gil (1933–2023) borrowed the form of geopolitics while inverting its substance. Where conventional geopolitics casts the peninsula as a marginal weak state hemmed in by surrounding powers, Kang — starting from his reading of Yu Kil-chun — accepted the historical reality of maritime–continental rivalry but made the reduction of tension between those forces, rather than alignment with one of them, the content of Korean strategy.

entries.title: 달의 뒷면 — '태평양 연구자'로서 브루스 커밍스 [The Far Side of the Moon: Bruce Cumings as a 'Pacific Researcher']
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Reframes Bruce Cumings as a scholar of the Pacific rather than only a historian of the Korean War, tracing his Peace Corps service, his area-studies doctoral training and his Seattle-based Pacific studies to argue that a vision of a peaceful Pacific international politics underlies the work usually read as Korean War revisionism.

entries.authors: 오드 아르네 웨스타 (Odd Arne Westad); 유강은 (translator); 옥창준 (해제 / critical afterword)
entries.title: 해제 [Critical afterword] to 『냉전 — 우리 시대를 만든 냉전의 세계사』 [The Cold War: A World History]
entries.venue: 서해문집 (Seohaemunjip)
entries.summary: Ok's afterword to the Korean edition of Westad's global history of the Cold War, extending his argument that the Cold War is better read as a newly opened world-historical space than as a bounded superpower confrontation.

entries.authors: Patrick Thaddeus Jackson and Sujin Heo
entries.title: Constructivism
entries.venue: Richard Devetak and Daniel R. McCarthy (eds.), An Introduction to International Relations, 4th edition (Cambridge University Press)
entries.summary: The constructivism chapter of a leading undergraduate IR textbook (4th edition, 2024). CAUTION: neither the publisher nor Crossref supplies an abstract and I could not fetch the chapter text, so no argument summary is asserted here. Given the co-authorship with Jackson, the chapter is presumed to present constructivism as a claim about the social constitution of actors, interests and rules rather than as a rival substantive theory alongside realism and liberalism — but this should be checked against the chapter before being quoted on a website.

entries.title: 한국화하는 국제정치학 — 한국국제정치학회의 초기 활동을 중심으로 [Koreanizing International Politics: Focusing on the Early Activities of the Korean Association of International Studies (KAIS)]
entries.venue: 역사문제연구 (Critical Studies on Modern Korean History)
entries.summary: Argues that the founding decade of the Korean Association of International Studies should be read not as institutional history but as the 'Koreanization of knowledge': under Lee Yong-hee's presidency, conferences on nationalism and modernization served as the machinery through which Western IR concepts were localized and made to speak to Korean circumstances.

entries.title: 외교사라는 서사 만들기 — 신기석과 탈식민 한국외교사 연구의 성립 사정 [Making a National Narrative of Diplomatic History: Focusing on Shin Ki-suk's Work on the Diplomatic History of Modern Korea]
entries.venue: 아세아연구 亞細亞硏究 (The Journal of Asiatic Studies), Asiatic Research Institute, Korea University
entries.summary: Argues that post-liberation Korean diplomatic history was constrained less by colonial-era neglect of the subject than by the absence of a sovereign state capable of conducting diplomacy at all. Through the Keijō Imperial University graduate Shin Ki-suk, Ok traces the passage from 'diplomatic history without diplomacy' to 'diplomatic history with diplomacy,' showing how Korean researchers built a narrative organized around sovereignty and self-determination.

entries.title: '잊힌 전쟁'과 '알려지지 않은 전쟁' 사이에서 — 미국 학계의 한국전쟁 연구 동향과 미국 한국학 [Between the 'Forgotten War' and the 'Unknown War': Trends in Korean War Studies in American Academia and American Korean Studies]
entries.venue: 한국사학사학보 (The Korean Journal of the History of Historiography)
entries.summary: Argues that American writing on the Korean War moved from a Far Eastern geopolitical frame that barely registered Korean actors to a Korea-centred one only as American Korean studies matured as a field, and that post-Cold War scholarship then split into an 'international turn' powered by declassified documents and a 'socio-cultural turn' built on collaboration with South Korean historians — a split that reshaped how the war is remembered.

entries.title: 출연(出捐)의 대가 — '과학기술'에서 '국가과학기술'로 [The Price of Contribution: From 'Science and Technology' to 'National' Science and Technology]
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Argues that Korea's government-funded research institutes were disciplined asymmetrically after the research councils were created in the late 1990s: science-and-technology councils were placed under strong state management in the name of national development, while humanities and social-science councils oscillated between servicing state projects and articulating a comprehensive national strategy. Ok identifies 2004 — the return of the S&T council to the Ministry of Science and Technology — as the decisive turn toward a 'national' research system.

entries.title: 경제·인문사회연구회를 통해 본 한국형 국책연구기관의 역사 — 경로, 정체성, 비교지평 [The History of Korean-style National Research Institutes seen through the National Research Council for Economics, Humanities and Social Sciences: Path, Identity, Comparative Horizon] (special issue introduction)
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Ok's framing essay for the special issue he organized on Korea's state-funded research institutes, proposing that they be analyzed along three axes — institutional path dependence, contested identity, and comparison with foreign models — rather than as a purely administrative story.

entries.authors: 존 J. 미어샤이머, 서배스천 로사토 (John J. Mearsheimer and Sebastian Rosato); 권지현 (translator); 옥창준 (해제 / critical afterword)
entries.title: 해제 [Critical afterword] to 『국가는 어떻게 생각하는가』 [How States Think: The Rationality of Foreign Policy]
entries.venue: 서해문집 (Seohaemunjip)
entries.summary: Ok supplied the scholarly afterword situating Mearsheimer and Rosato's defence of state rationality for Korean readers — one of a series of commissioned framing essays through which he introduces major Anglophone IR and Cold War works into Korean debate.

entries.title: On being Chinese and being complexified: Chinese IR as a transcultural project
entries.venue: Review of International Studies
entries.summary: Argues that a distinctive and durable Chinese IR is possible only if it abandons the national-school project that equates Chineseness with Chinese national culture, and adopts instead a non-national, non-essentialized transcultural conception of Chineseness. Chineseness, Choi shows, has always been a fiction of privileged descent from antiquity that rival claimants redefined; the shi elites in particular made it an aspirational ethos that absorbed foreign influences and thereby became transcultural. Drawing on the ontological turn and Roy Wagner's anthropology, he further recasts Chineseness as immanent humanity, which dissolves the innate-nature/constructed-culture divide. Such a Chinese IR would complexify its own tradition internally and other IR traditions externally, advancing the pluralization of the discipline.

entries.title: 냉전 초기 한국의 지정학 서사 — 숙명의 지정학에서 운명의 지정학으로 [From Fate to Destiny: The Making of a Geopolitical Narrative in Post-colonial and Cold War South Korea]
entries.venue: 개념과 소통 (Concepts and Communication), Hallym Academy of Sciences
entries.summary: Argues that early Cold War South Korean intellectuals appropriated Japanese and German geopolitics inherited from the colonial period and converted a geography of 'fate' (숙명) into one of 'destiny' (운명) — a position alterable through power relations rather than fixed by environment. Ok calls this a Koreanization of geopolitics: a geopolitics of the weak that contests the predetermined spatial hierarchies written from great-power vantage points, and that later framed the reception of Anglo-American political geography in the 1960s.

entries.title: 이선근의 1930~1940년대 역사 해석과 '조선 정신' [Lee Seon-geun's Historical Interpretation in the 1930s–1940s and the 'Korean Spirit']
entries.venue: 동북아역사논총 (Northeast Asian History Review), Northeast Asian History Foundation
entries.summary: Argues that Lee Seon-geun's writings — his Contemporary History of Korea (1931/1945) and Studies on Hwarangdo (1949) — should be read as a continuous body of historical thought rather than as political opportunism. Lee located a 'Korean spirit' expressed ideologically in Donghak and politically in the Daewongun's policies, pursued Korean identity inside the Japanese empire in the 1930s, and after liberation redeployed the same framework to give the divided South's founding a genealogical legitimacy against the crisis of partition.

entries.authors: 옥창준 (Chang Joon Ok), with 기유정, 김태진, 이경미, 장세진, 장인성, 장진성
entries.title: 냉전의 '현실'을 포착하는 두 시각 [Two Perspectives for Capturing the 'Reality' of the Cold War] (ch. 6)
entries.venue: 『이용희의 정치학과 정치사상』 [The Political Science and Political Thought of Lee Yong-hee], 연암서가 (Yeonamseoga)
entries.summary: In the first collective scholarly reassessment of Dongju Lee Yong-hee, Ok's chapter sets Cho Hyowon's and Lee's rival readings of Cold War 'reality' side by side to argue that Korean IR's founding moment turned on a contest over how to describe Korea's position, not on a contest between Western and indigenous knowledge.

entries.authors: Patrick Thaddeus Jackson and Sujin Heo
entries.title: Working on relationalism
entries.venue: New Perspectives: Interdisciplinary Journal of Central & East European Politics and International Relations (Sage)
entries.summary: Argues that the standard framing of the relational turn — a binary choice between substantialism and relationalism, or between dualist and nondual/incarnational sensibilities — is insufficient. Every attempt to translate a relational or nondual sensibility into the scholarly form of life runs into characteristic problems, the essay contends, precisely because the practice of scholarly writing is itself always already inclined toward a more dualist way of going on. Relationalism is thus reframed as ongoing labour against the grain of one's own medium rather than as a position one can simply adopt. The essay appears in a special section of New Perspectives 30(2), 'Relationality in Central and Eastern Europe' (introduced by Nicholas Michelsen), alongside contributions by Emilian Kavalski, Charlotte Epstein, Amaya Querejazu and Milja Kurki.

entries.title: 냉전 초기 한국 국제정치 지식의 재구성 [The Reconfiguration of Knowledge about International Politics in Korea in the Early Cold War]
entries.venue: Ph.D. dissertation, Graduate School, Seoul National University (Dept. of Political Science and International Relations, International Relations major)
entries.summary: Argues that the making of international-politics knowledge in Korea between liberation and the mid-1960s was not the transplantation or 'Americanization' of US social science but a reconstruction: Korean scholars recombined geopolitical discourse, imported IR theory and international-society frameworks — including legacies of the Japanese imperial knowledge order — into an order of knowledge fitted to Korea's own positional predicament. The dissertation reframes the history of Korean IR as a history of Korean intellectuals reinterpreting reality rather than receiving it.

entries.title: 한국학의 위상학 — 한국에서 열린 최초의 한국학 국제학술회의('한국의 전통과 변천', 1969)를 중심으로 [Topology of Korean Studies: Focusing on the Conference on Tradition and Change in Korea, 1969]
entries.venue: 한국학 (Korean Studies Quarterly), Academy of Korean Studies
entries.summary: Argues that the first international Korean studies conference held in Korea — the 1969 'Tradition and Change in Korea' meeting jointly organized by Korea University's Asiatic Research Center and American institutions — was the point where two separate currents converged: a domestic drive to project national studies abroad and an American accumulation of Korea expertise. Korean participants pressed for independence from Chinese and Japanese studies and searched Korean tradition for modernization potential, while social scientists brought fieldwork on contemporary change.

entries.title: 현실로서의 냉전과 한국 국제정치학의 형성 — 조효원과 이용희의 냉전 국제정치론을 중심으로 ['Realistic' Visions of the Cold War: Hyowon Cho and Yonghee Lee's Frame on International Politics and the Cold War]
entries.venue: 한국학연구 (Korean Studies), Institute of Korean Studies, Inha University
entries.summary: Rejects the received contrast between Cho Hyowon as a derivative importer of Western IR and Lee Yong-hee as an indigenous theorist, arguing that both mobilized American international relations knowledge to capture Korea's Cold War predicament. Ok warns that the existing emphasis on the origin of concepts becomes dogmatic when it demands that Korean theory be derived only from Korean experience, and proposes instead studying how scholars actively deployed imported intellectual tools.

entries.authors: 백승욱, 왕후이, 백지운, 옥창준, 이일영 (authors); 백원담 (ed.)
entries.title: Chapter in 『1919와 1949 — 21세기 한·중 '역사 다시 쓰기'와 '다른 세계'』 [1919 and 1949: Twenty-first-century Korean-Chinese 'Rewriting of History' and 'Another World']
entries.venue: 진인진 (Jininjin), Sungkonghoe University Institute for East Asian Studies, China Issues series 1
entries.summary: Contributes to a Korean–Chinese collaborative volume (with Wang Hui among the authors) that uses the twin anniversaries of 1919 and 1949 to ask what a rewriting of modern East Asian history from within the region — rather than from the Cold War's inherited categories — would look like.

entries.title: 이론의 종속과 종속의 이론 — 1970년대 중반~1980년대 한국 사회과학 학계와 종속이론 [Dependency of Theory and the Theory of Dependency: Korean Social Scientists and Dependency Theory in the mid-1970s–1980s]
entries.venue: 역사문제연구 (Critical Studies on Modern Korean History)
entries.summary: Argues that Korean social scientists caught between a state suspicious of dependency theory's Marxism and student activists convinced of its universality succeeded in criticizing Marxist dependency theory from Korean experience, but never resolved the prior and deeper problem the debate had raised — the 'dependency of theory' itself, that is, the absence of autonomous Korean social-scientific frameworks.

entries.title: 지역질서 연구를 위한 구성주의 방법론 검토 [Constructivist Methodology Revisited for Regional Order Studies]
entries.venue: 전재성 외 [Chaesung Chun and Kiyoung Chang (eds.)], 『동아시아 지역질서의 보편과 특수: 이론과 현실』 [Universals and Particulars of Regional Order in East Asia: Theory and Practice] (서울: 사회평론아카데미 / Sahoipyoungnon Academy)
entries.summary: A methodological review chapter asking what constructivism can and cannot deliver when the object of study is a regional order rather than an individual state's behaviour. CAUTION: this summary is inferred from the title and the volume's framing (universals vs. particulars in East Asian regional order) — I could not obtain the chapter's text or the volume's chapter-level table of contents, so the argument should be verified before publication. The volume itself is confirmed: 사회평론아카데미, 20 June 2018, ISBN 9791188108718, marketed as '전재성 외' (Chun Chaesung et al.).

entries.title: 이용희의 지식 체계 형성과 한국 국제정치학의 재구성 [Lee Yong-hee as 'Bricoleur': The Birth of 'International Politics' in 1950s Korea]
entries.venue: 사이間SAI, International Association of Korean Literary and Cultural Studies
entries.summary: Argues that Lee Yong-hee (Dongju), the founding figure of Korean IR, did not import American international relations wholesale but performed an intellectual bricolage — repurposing colonial-era knowledge and available conceptual materials alongside American social science to assemble a distinctly Korean 'international politics' in the 1950s. Reframes the founding of the discipline as reconstruction rather than reception.

entries.title: 냉전과 인터넷 커뮤니케이션의 구조: 정보기술의 국제정치적 구성 [The Cold War and the Communication Structure of the Internet: The Constitution of IT through International Politics]
entries.venue: 세계정치 [World Politics] 18호 『커뮤니케이션 세계정치』, 김상배 편, 서울대학교 국제문제연구소 (Institute of International Studies, Seoul National University)
entries.summary: Inverts the usual causal story in which information technology is an exogenous variable acting on world politics, arguing instead that the Internet's architecture was itself constituted by international politics. Choi shows the Internet has a double communication structure — radically decentralized routing governed by centrally controlled protocols — and that this duality was engineered to satisfy the technical requirements of U.S. nuclear strategy under Cold War constraints, while the development process was in turn shaped by the material properties of the technology. Case studies of the SAGE air-defense system (1950s) and ARPANET (1960s) trace the constitutive interaction of Cold War system, U.S. strategic need, and IT's material features.

entries.title: 식민지 조선의 국제주의 [Internationalism in Colonial Korea]
entries.venue: 하영선·손열 편 [Young-Sun Ha and Yul Sohn (eds.)], 근대한국의 사회과학 개념 형성사 2 [Conceptual History of Social Science in Modern Korea, vol. 2], Paju: Changbi
entries.summary: A conceptual-history chapter tracing how 'internationalism' was received, translated, and put to work in colonial Korea, situating the term within the Ha/Sohn project on how core social-scientific concepts travelled into and were reworked by modern Korean thought. NOTE: verified from Kwon's CV; the volume exists and is edited by Ha and Sohn, but the chapter title is a back-translation of the CV's romanized entry and the table of contents could not be independently retrieved.

entries.title: 웹 2.0과 인권 네트워크의 세계정치: 국제앰네스티의 사례 [Web 2.0 and World Politics of Human Rights Networks: The Case of Amnesty International]
entries.venue: 김상배 편 [Sangbae Kim (ed.)], 거미줄 치기와 벌집 짓기: 네트워크 이론으로 보는 세계정치의 변환 [Spinning Webs and Building Hives: Transformation of World Politics in the Framework of Network Theory], Paju: Hanul
entries.summary: Argues, within Sangbae Kim's network-theory framework, that transnational civil networks such as Amnesty International have been reshaped by Web 2.0 not only in organizational form but in the content of human rights discourse itself -- the 'hive-building' side of the volume's web-spinning/hive-building distinction. NOTE: chapter attribution to 권민주 was corroborated by a description of the volume's structure in search results, but the printed table of contents was not directly retrieved; exact chapter title and pages should be confirmed.

themes.title: The Asian Cold War: Non-Alignment, Division, and the Korean War
themes.blurb: Recovers the Asian Cold War as a field of live alternatives rather than a settled bipolar script: Bandung and neutrality as options South Korean and North Korean elites weighed, rival 1949 and 1954 designs for a Pacific alliance against Nehruvian non-alignment, North Korea's imaginative geography of the Third World, and the divergent nationalisms that reorganized two anti-communist states after democratization. Korean War historiography belongs here too, as the contest over who gets to narrate the war that fixed the division.

entries.authors: 옥창준 (Chang Joon Ok), in 정용욱 외 (eds.)
entries.title: 냉전기 북한의 상상 지리와 '평양 선언' [North Korea's Imaginative Geography and the 'Pyongyang Declaration' in the Cold War] (Part 1, ch. 9)
entries.venue: 『오늘의 한국 현대사 2 — 분단과 냉전』 [Korean Contemporary History Today 2: Division and the Cold War], 푸른역사 (Purunyeoksa)
entries.summary: Chapter version of Ok's argument that North Korea built a spatial self-understanding through Afro-Asian solidarity and non-alignment, placed within a seventeen-author survey of division and the Cold War aimed at a wider readership.
themes: North Korea and the Third World

entries.authors: 옥창준 (Chang Joon Ok), with 공임순, 김나현, 남현지, 박연희, 송은영, 이성주, 이철호, 장세진, 조송이, 조은애, 최진석
entries.title: 냉전기 한국 지식인의 아시아 아프리카 상상 [Korean Intellectuals' Asian–African Imagination in the Cold War] (Part 1, ch. 4)
entries.venue: 『청맥』의 시간들 — 1960년대 한국의 지식장과 탈냉전의 아포리아 [The Times of Ch'ŏngmaek: Korea's Intellectual Field in the 1960s and the Aporia of the Post-Cold War], 소명출판 (Somyong)
entries.summary: Ok's chapter in a twelve-author study of the 1960s journal Ch'ŏngmaek, arguing that the Afro-Asian horizon opened to Korean intellectuals after Bandung was read back through national interest rather than solidarity — a limit the volume treats as the aporia of Korea's attempted exit from the Cold War.

entries.title: '동맹'과 '비동맹'의 각축 — 1954년 제네바, 콜롬보, 보고르 [The Competition of Alliance and Non-alignment: Geneva, Colombo and Bogor, 1954]
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Argues that the Asian Cold War order between the 1953 armistice and the 1955 Bandung Conference was set by a collision between Syngman Rhee's anti-communist alliance drive and the Nehru-led project of peaceful coexistence and non-alignment, and reconstructs that collision across the successive 1954 conferences at Geneva, Colombo, Jinhae, Manila and Bogor.

entries.title: [기획의 말] 해방 80년, 반둥 70년: 냉전기 아시아의 중립·비동맹의 역사와 평화의 상상력 [Editor's Introduction — 80 Years since Liberation, 70 Years since Bandung: Histories of Neutrality and Non-alignment in Cold War Asia and the Imagination of Peace]
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Ok's introduction to the special issue he organized, arguing that pairing the eightieth anniversary of liberation with the seventieth of Bandung recovers neutrality and non-alignment as live options in Cold War Asia and thereby restores an imaginative resource for thinking peace today.

entries.title: 러시아의 백년 전쟁 — 크림전쟁과 한국전쟁 [Russia's Hundred-Year War: The Crimean War and the Korean War]
entries.venue: 동북아 역사 포커스 (Northeast Asian History Focus), Northeast Asian History Foundation
entries.summary: Places the Crimean War and the Korean War inside a single long Russian eastward trajectory, arguing that a 'waiting policy' running toward the Pacific and Stalin's postwar vision for Asia — rather than a sudden 1950 decision — explain the resolve to go to war, and drawing the comparison out to present memory seventy-five years on.

entries.title: 국제적 시각으로 본 전쟁 — 『한국전란1년지』 다시 읽기 [The War Seen Internationally: Rereading the Record of One Year of the Korean War]
entries.venue: 동북아역사리포트 (Northeast Asian History Report), Northeast Asian History Foundation
entries.summary: Rereads the South Korean government's official first-year chronicle of the Korean War to argue that the state framed the conflict as an international war from the outset, and that the compilation itself was an instrument of that framing.

entries.title: 냉전기 통일 베트남의 국제정치 인식의 전환: 공산당 전당대회 보고서와 Tạp chí Cộng sản을 중심으로 [Unified Vietnam's Evolving View of International Politics During the Cold War: An Analysis of National Congress Political Reports and Tạp chí Cộng sản Articles]
entries.venue: 아세아연구 [The Journal of Asiatic Studies, Asiatic Research Institute, Korea University]
entries.summary: Argues that unified Vietnam's foreign policy in 1976-1990 is better explained by a shift in how the Party leadership read the structure of international politics than by its bilateral quarrels with China, the USSR or the US. Reading the Fourth, Fifth and Sixth Party Congress political reports alongside a decade of Tạp chí Cộng sản, Song shows that the late-1970s frame of 'socialism versus capitalism and reaction' — which prescribed solidarity with Moscow against Beijing and Washington — gave way by the mid-1980s to an 'economic internationalism' that admitted the possibility of socialist-capitalist cooperation. Đổi mới, on this account, followed from a reinterpretation of the international system rather than from economic necessity alone, while Vietnam still framed its diplomacy in socialist terms and sought strategic balance between the superpowers.

entries.title: 경합하는 '태평양' 구상 — 1949년 태평양 '동맹'의 재해석 [Competing 'Pacific' Visions: A Reinterpretation of the 1949 Pacific 'Alliance']
entries.venue: 역사연구 (The Journal of History), Institute for Historical Studies
entries.summary: Argues that the 1949 Pacific alliance proposals have been misread as an episode in ROK–US bilateral relations or as a failed Asian NATO, and should instead be placed inside an Asian Cold War in which three regional projects competed: India's post-1947 non-alignment, the alliance-seeking of Syngman Rhee's Korea and the KMT regime, and the Philippines' federation model. These rivalries, Ok shows, resurface after the Korean War.

entries.authors: 옥창준 (Chang Joon Ok), with 신욱희, 구갑우, 오정현, 이혜정, 량미화, 은용수
entries.title: 경합하는 '태평양' 구상: 1949년 태평양 '동맹'의 재해석 [Competing 'Pacific' Visions: Reinterpreting the 1949 Pacific 'Alliance'] (opening chapter)
entries.venue: 『한반도 국제관계사의 재인식』 [Reconsidering the International Relations History of the Korean Peninsula], 사회평론아카데미 (Sahoepyeongnon Academy)
entries.summary: Opens a collective volume that rereads the international history of the divided peninsula — San Francisco, the 1954 Geneva conference, the 1954 ROK–US Agreed Minutes, the Sino-Soviet-DPRK triangle, postcolonial theory — with Ok's chapter arguing that 1949's Pacific alliance schemes belong to an Asian Cold War of competing regional projects rather than to a US-centred alliance narrative.

entries.title: 한국전쟁과 복권: 애국복권 입법 [The Korean War and Lottery: The Legislation of the Patriotic Lottery]
entries.venue: 사회와역사 [Society and History / Korean Social History Association]
entries.summary: Argues that South Korea's Patriotic Lottery (1951-1957) was legitimated through a deliberate double framing: proponents in the government and National Assembly justified state-run gambling both instrumentally, as a rational wartime device to absorb idle capital and curb inflation, and morally, by recasting ticket-buying as a voluntary, collective act of patriotism that let ordinary citizens share in solving the fiscal crisis. The authors show that the scheme collapsed when both frames failed at once — weak sales destroyed the rational-instrumental case, while coercive selling and fraud in the administering agency revived the moral objection to state-sponsored gambling. The paper positions itself as the first systematic study of the Patriotic Lottery and a contribution to fiscal sociology.

entries.title: 냉전기 북한의 상상 지리와 '평양 선언' [Pyongyang Declarations: The Imaginative Geography of North Korea during the Cold War]
entries.venue: 통일과 평화 (Journal of Peace and Unification Studies), Institute for Peace and Unification Studies, Seoul National University
entries.summary: Argues that the Cold War should be treated not as a closed interpretive period ending in 1991 but as a space newly opened after 1945, and reads the Pyongyang Declarations issued at the 1964 and 1981 conferences to show how North Korea built an imaginative geography of itself through Afro-Asian solidarity, non-alignment and Third World engagement — and how that spatial self-understanding shifted between the two moments.
themes: North Korea and the Third World

entries.authors: 옥창준, 최규진 (Chang Joon Ok and Choi Kyu-jin)
entries.title: 이정식과 브루스 커밍스 저술에 대한 대위법(對位法)적 독해 [A Contrapuntal Reading of the Writings of Chong-Sik Lee and Bruce Cumings]
entries.venue: 사림 (The Historical Journal), Susun Historical Society
entries.summary: Argues that Chong-Sik Lee and Bruce Cumings — the two founding figures of American Korean studies — should be read contrapuntally rather than adjudicated between: Lee derives North Korea from the historical fusion of Korean nationalism with communism and concludes Soviet intervention was necessary to its founding, while Cumings casts the US military government as counterrevolutionary and the 1950 war as the eruption of colonial Korea's contradictions. Reading them together, the authors claim, opens a better view of the interconnected histories of Asia than either account alone.

entries.title: 남방정책의 계보학 — 아세아민족반공연맹부터 신남방정책까지 [A Genealogy of the Southern Policy: From the Asian People's Anti-Communist League to the New Southern Policy]
entries.venue: 황해문화 (Hwanghae Review), Saeol Cultural Foundation
entries.summary: Reconstructs a genealogy running from the 1954 Asian People's Anti-Communist League to the Moon government's New Southern Policy, arguing that South Korea's successive turns 'southward' have been shaped less by fresh economic opportunity than by an inherited Cold War repertoire of anti-communist regional organizing, and that the distance between Korea and Asia has been reproduced rather than closed by these initiatives.

entries.title: 반공국가의 위기와 민족주의의 부상 — 민주화 이후 한국의 대북정책과 대만의 대중정책에 관한 비교 [The Crisis of Anti-Communist States and the Rise of Nationalism: A Comparative Study on South Korea's North Policy and Taiwan's China Policy after Democratization]
entries.venue: 세계정치 (Journal of World Politics), 서울대학교 국제문제연구소 [Institute of International Affairs, Seoul National University]
entries.summary: Asks why two structurally similar divided states diverged after their first horizontal transfers of power, and argues that the answer lies in the different nationalisms that surfaced during democratization rather than in security structure. In South Korea the re-emergence of ethnic nationalism recoded North Korea as an in-group member of the same national community, which underwrote the Kim Dae-jung government's reconciliation and cooperation policy; in Taiwan the rise of civic nationalism, stressing political rather than ethnic difference, recoded China as an authoritarian out-group threatening Taiwanese democracy, which enabled the Chen Shui-bian government's independence-oriented line and sharpened tension across the Strait.
themes: divided states and the Cold War

entries.authors: 옥창준, 김민환 (Chang Joon Ok and Kim Min Hwan)
entries.title: 사상심리전의 텍스트로서 한국전쟁 — 자유세계로의 확산과 동아시아적 귀환 [The Korean War as a Text of Ideological Psychological Warfare: Dissemination to the Free World and East Asian Return]
entries.venue: 역사비평 (Critical Review of History)
entries.summary: Follows the 1951 propaganda book 'The Reds Take a City' as it was produced, altered, translated and finally re-imported into South Korea via East Asia, arguing that knowledge produced in Seoul was folded into a regional anti-communist psychological-warfare apparatus. The article shows a localized Korean War narrative acquiring 'the universality of the global Cold War' through multilingual circulation — and returning home, as a comic, in a form markedly different from the South Korean original.

entries.title: 윌리엄 스툭의 국제전 접근법과 한국전쟁 연구 [William Stueck and the Korean War]
entries.venue: 미국학 (American Studies), Institute of American Studies, Seoul National University
entries.summary: Argues that Korean scholarship has flattened William Stueck into the 'traditionalist' foil to Bruce Cumings' revisionism, and that this binary misreads him. Ok contends Stueck's decisive contribution is his critical examination of US policy toward Korea before June 1950, an argument that cuts across the traditionalism/revisionism divide and recovers dimensions of the war's origins that both camps overlooked.

entries.title: 냉전기 한국 지식인의 아시아 상상 [Korean Intellectuals' Imagination of Asia during the Cold War]
entries.venue: M.A. thesis, Graduate School, Seoul National University
entries.summary: Traces how South Korean intellectuals of the 1950s–60s constructed 'Asia' as an object of political rather than merely cultural imagination, arguing that the widening of their horizon beyond the bipolar Cold War did not produce Third World solidarity but a reading of Asia through South Korean national interest. Formed the basis of his 2015 journal article on Asian–African imagination.

entries.title: 냉전기 한국 지식인의 아시아 아프리카 상상 [Korean Intellectuals' Asian–African Imagination in the Cold War Period]
entries.venue: 한국문화연구 (The Korean Cultural Studies), Ewha Womans University
entries.summary: Argues that the 1955 Bandung Conference let a postcolonial consciousness suppressed by the Korean War resurface, converting 'the Orient' from a cultural into a political concept usable to explain Asian and African nationalism. But it shows that Korean intellectuals read Afro-Asian currents overwhelmingly through the frame of national interest rather than solidarity, a tendency that hardened after 1965 as international Afro-Asian solidarity itself declined.

entries.title: 미국으로 간 "반둥 정신" — 체스터 보울즈의 제3세계 [The "Bandung Spirit" in Cold War United States: The Third Worldism of Chester Bowles]
entries.venue: 사회와 역사 (Society and History), Korean Social History Association
entries.summary: Argues that Chester Bowles domesticated the 'Bandung spirit' inside American Cold War liberalism by reading a shared anti-colonial experience between the United States and newly independent Asia, most concretely during his ambassadorship to India from 1951. It shows that this culturally relativist Third Worldism was displaced in the 1960s by Walt Rostow's modernization theory, and that the American reception of Bandung therefore narrowed rather than widened.

entries.title: 남북대화 규범의 탄생 — 구성주의 시각에서 본 1970년대 남북대화 [Inter-Korean Talks as an Emerging Norm: A Constructivist Perspective on the North-South Korea Talks in the 1970s]
entries.venue: 한국정치외교사논총 [Korean Journal of Political and Diplomatic History]
entries.summary: Argues that realism cannot explain why the two Koreas began talking in 1971 and keeps talking about talking afterwards, and offers a constructivist account instead: the talks emerged where long-held commitments to 'nationalism' (a single Korean nation) and 'humanitarianism' (reuniting separated families) converged under détente, values that pre-existed the opening but could not be acted on while Cold War structures held. Song shows that although the substance collapsed by 1973 over unification method — improvements resting on tactical policy shifts rather than on redefined interests or identity — both regimes thereafter competed to claim the 'spirit of dialogue' and to blame the other for breakdown, which is precisely the behaviour that reveals inter-Korean dialogue had become a norm both sides were obliged to profess.

themes.title: Power Transition, War, and Maritime Order
themes.blurb: The collective's security wing, built on the claim that transitions are decided by how a leading sea power redraws its first line of defense and by whether smaller states can convert exposure into leverage — not by aggregate capability curves. It runs from Fashoda, the July Crisis and Roosevelt's Pacific to the U.S.–China naval shift, shipbuilding statecraft and the 'unstable hybrid order' that middle powers now have to navigate, and it keeps secondary-state agency, not great-power intention, at the centre.

entries.authors: Jaeyoung Kim and Zhen Arc Han
entries.title: Crisis and Economic Interdependence: Regional Order and Peaceful Change in the Asia-Pacific
entries.venue: Book chapter, under review
entries.summary: Listed as a book chapter under review on Kim's June 2026 CV, co-authored with Zhen (Arc) Han (Assistant Professor of Government, Sacred Heart University; McGill Ph.D., who works on economic interdependence and rising-power behaviour). The title points to how crises stress economic interdependence and what that implies for peaceful change in Asia-Pacific regional order. Argument unverified.

entries.title: Conclusion: Rethinking Great Powers, Regions, and Peaceful Change in the New Cold War Era
entries.venue: The New Cold War and the Remaking of Regions, edited by T. V. Paul and Markus Kornprobst (Washington, DC: Georgetown University Press)
entries.summary: Concluding chapter of a volume whose premise is that the present 'New Cold War' is not a replay of bipolarity but plays out in a multipolar and 'multiplex' setting, where secondary states and regional actors align their interests strategically with rival great powers rather than simply being absorbed into blocs. Krickovic and Kim draw the volume's realist, liberal and constructivist contributions together to reassess the relationship between great powers, regional ordering, and the prospects for peaceful versus violent change. NOTE: summary reconstructed from the publisher's volume description and the chapter's stated role in the book; the chapter text is paywalled (JSTOR/Georgetown UP) and was not read.

entries.title: 1차 세계대전 원인론에 대한 다른 시선: 세르비아를 둘러싼 오스트리아-헝가리 제국의 군사력 사용의지와 러시아의 군사동원, 1908-1914 [A Different Perspective on the Causes of the First World War: Austria-Hungary's Resolve to Use Force against Serbia and Russia's Military Mobilizations, 1908-1914]
entries.venue: 한국정치외교사논총 (Journal of Korean Political and Diplomatic History)
entries.summary: Oh asks why the July 1914 crisis escalated into a continental war when the structurally similar Balkan crises of 1908-1913 did not. Tracing variation in two interacting variables — Austria-Hungary's resolve to use military force against Serbia, and Russia's decisions on preparatory war measures and mobilization — he argues that it was the interaction between Vienna's heightened resolve and St. Petersburg's mobilization choices between 25 and 30 July that constituted the immediate precipitating cause. The article thereby supplements and moves beyond the dominant 'German paradigm' that assigns causal primacy to Berlin.

entries.title: The agency of secondary states in order transition in the Indo-Pacific
entries.venue: The Pacific Review
entries.summary: Argues that secondary states — all states weaker or smaller than the hegemon and the rising challenger — are not merely pawns of great powers but can convert their exposed position into leverage, and thereby help shape the contours of US–China competition and of the emerging Indo-Pacific order. Faults the order-transition literature for a preoccupation with great-power politics that leaves 'agency' both neglected and conceptually vague, and proposes an analytical framework that disaggregates agency along three dimensions: the motivation behind it, the type of resources mobilized, and the availability of partners.

entries.title: An Interactive Theory of Power Projection: Naval Power Shift, The Contagion Effect, and Alignment Opportunity
entries.venue: Ph.D. dissertation, Department of Political Science, Morrissey College of Arts and Sciences, Boston College
entries.summary: Oh argues that neither balance-of-power nor hegemonic-shift theory explains why leading sea powers and naval challengers sometimes fight despite power disparity and distance, and sometimes settle despite parity and proximity. He builds a mid-range 'interactive theory of power projection' in which the outcome of a naval power shift turns on two conditions: the interaction between a challenger's expansion and the leading sea power's expectations about the *contagion effect* on its first line of maritime defense (that an occupation becomes a stepping stone, produces negative second-order effects on a distant defense line, or strips away local allies), and whether *alignment opportunity* — set by third-party common threats and available allies in the theater — is open or closed. Comparative historical case studies of two Anglo-French dyads (1856-1870, 1882-1904) and the U.S.-Japan dyad (1921-1941) generate the framework, which he then applies to the U.S.-China case. Permanent handle: http://hdl.handle.net/2345/bc-ir:109936.

entries.title: 흔들리는 '언덕 위의 도성' — 미국-이스라엘의 특별한 관계사 [The Trembling 'City upon a Hill': A History of the Special US–Israel Relationship]
entries.venue: 황해문화 (Hwanghae Review), Saeol Cultural Foundation
entries.summary: A historical essay arguing that the US–Israel 'special relationship' was underwritten by an American self-image of the redeemer nation — the 'city upon a hill' — and that the Gaza war has destabilized the moral narrative on which that relationship rested.

entries.title: 7월 위기와 1차 세계대전 발발 원인에 대한 재고찰: 독일과 러시아의 위협인식 [The July Crisis and the Causes of the First World War Revisited: Civil-Military Threat Perceptions of Germany and Russia]
entries.venue: 군사 (Gunsa / Military History), Institute for Military History Compilation, ROK Ministry of National Defense
entries.summary: Oh argues that the long-running debate over July 1914 has been muddled because scholars treat 'Germany' and 'Russia' as unitary actors rather than separating civilian from military threat perceptions. Disaggregating the two, he shows that Germany's 'blank check' rested on the civilian assumption of a rapid, localized Austrian settlement with Serbia, while Russian preparatory mobilization — which Sazonov initiated as deterrence without grasping that the measures encompassed deployments on the German frontier — sharply intensified German *military* threat perception. The escalation into continental war thus turned on an intelligence-mediated civil-military perception gap, which challenges the traditional German-responsibility paradigm.

themes.title: Planetary Order, Climate, and the Terms of Peace
themes.blurb: Asks what kind of order the Anthropocene demands once nature stops being the passive object of politics — reworking Teilhard's noosphere through Neo-Confucian theory into a post-sovereign 'Republic of the Noosphere', reading historical power transitions as contests of adaptability under ecological pressure, and proposing planetary coevolution as a strategy for everyone who is not one of the two superpowers. It is the collective's most explicitly normative front, where 'decent peace' is judged insufficient for an era of systemic transformation.

entries.title: Historical Intersections of Climatic Change and Power Transitions: Ecological Pressure, Differential Adaptability, and the U.S.-China Power Transition in the Anthropocene
entries.venue: International Relations of the Asia-Pacific
entries.summary: Accepted and DOI-registered but not yet released (the DOI resolves to Crossref's 'pending publication' page as of August 2026), so no abstract is yet public. On the evidence of the title and the authors' own listing, the paper argues that climatic change and power transitions have historically intersected: ecological pressure does not affect all contenders equally but redistributes relative power according to states' differential capacity to adapt, and the authors extend this historical mechanism to the U.S.-China power transition under Anthropocene conditions.

entries.title: Historical Intersections of Climatic Change and Power Transitions: Ecological Pressure, Balance of Adaptability, and the U.S.-China Power Transition in the Anthropocene
entries.venue: International Relations of the Asia-Pacific (Oxford University Press)
entries.summary: Co-authored with Inho Choi, this article brings climatic change into power-transition theory by arguing that ecological pressure is a recurring driver of transition outcomes and that what determines who prevails is not raw material capability but a 'balance of adaptability' — the relative capacity of rival orders to absorb and reorganize under environmental stress. The authors read historical cases of climate-stressed transitions forward to the contemporary U.S.-China case in the Anthropocene. Listed as forthcoming on Oh's July 2026 CV; his March 2026 CV recorded it at Revise & Resubmit, so the acceptance is recent and no volume/DOI has been assigned yet.

entries.title: 인류세와 행성질서: 마음권의 공화국 [Planetary Order for the Anthropocene: Republic of the Noosphere]
entries.venue: 한국정치학회보 [Korean Political Science Review]
entries.summary: Contends that the Anthropocene is a cosmological transformation — nature and humanity are now interconnected rather than passive object and active subject — and that it therefore requires a corresponding transformation of order, a question IR has neglected by treating the Anthropocene mainly as an existential crisis. Choi takes Teilhard de Chardin's noosphere, the planetary sphere of mind that regulates all habitable zones, to derive the political and ethical principles such an order demands, then rebuilds the concept through Neo-Confucian political theory to propose a 'Republic of the Noosphere': a bottom-up, post-sovereign planetary republic in which individual minds across the planet unite while retaining their autonomy.

A disciplinary-history / theory piece reading the Seoul National University IR theorist Shin Wook-hee's work on role conception as a form of 'realist constructivism' — the one item in Kim's pipeline that speaks directly to the Korean IR canon and to the project of provincializing Anglophone IR. entries.venue: In progress

Co-authored with her dissertation co-chair Tanisha M. Fazal. NOTE: unpublished; no draft is publicly circulated.

entries.venue: Work in progress
